detail:
The Ehlers-Danlos Society is explicit about what researchers do not yet know about craniocervical instability (CCI) in the Ehlers-Danlos syndromes. The areas it lists as needing research are: how common CCI is in EDS; making sure methods for finding CCI in EDS are helpful; and development of an international data registry to help start trials for CCI therapy in EDS.

Those questions sit on top of a basic gap the Society also names: there are no established guidelines for treatment of CCI in EDS, and the information clinicians use is drawn from the diagnosis and treatment of CCI in various other connective tissue disorders. A registry that gathers comparable cases internationally is proposed as a step toward testing CCI therapies in EDS itself.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about craniocervical instability research.
summary: The Ehlers-Danlos Society lists the research questions craniocervical instability still raises in EDS: how common it is, making sure the methods for finding it are helpful, and developing an international data registry to help start trials of CCI therapy.
takeaways: how common cci is in eds is still unknown
validating the methods for finding cci is a stated research priority
an international registry is proposed to help start treatment trials
research participation is optional; talk to your doctor about studies
title: Craniocervical instability research: what still needs answering
